title: Mapping simplex as a pushout attaching the last fiber
statement:
Use small simplicial sets and standard simplices of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and colimits of [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Let $n>0$ and let $A_0\leftarrow\cdots\leftarrow A_n$ be any chain of small simplicial sets, with composites $t_{j,i}:A_j\to A_i$. Define the mapping simplex by $M(A)_r=\coprod_{\alpha:[r]\to[n]}(A_{\alpha(r)})_r$ and operators $(\alpha,a)\mapsto(\alpha\theta,t_{\alpha(r),\alpha\theta(s)}\theta^*a)$ for $\theta:[s]\to[r]$. Define $M_-=M(A_0\leftarrow\cdots\leftarrow A_{n-1})$ by the same formula, and let $T=\Delta^{\{0,\ldots,n-1\}}\subseteq\Delta^n$. Define $g:A_n\times T\to M_-$ in degree $r$ by $g(a,\alpha)=(\alpha,t_{n,\alpha(r)}a)$, and $h:A_n\times\Delta^n\to M(A)$ by $h(a,\alpha)=(\alpha,t_{n,\alpha(r)}a)$. Together with the inclusion $M_-\hookrightarrow M(A)$ these maps induce a canonical isomorphism of simplicial sets
$$M_-\amalg_{A_n\times T}(A_n\times\Delta^n)\ \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\ M(A).$$
It respects the maps to $\Delta^n$ and is natural for maps of chains that commute with all transitions. No injectivity or fibrancy hypothesis on the chain is required.

source.place: HTT Lemma 3.2.2.9, printed pp.182–183, first pushout diagram; the simplicial decomposition $M(\phi)=M(\phi')\amalg_{A_n\times T}(A_n\times\Delta^n)$ is stated verbatim in the proof of HTT Proposition 3.2.2.10, printed p.183 ("We note that M(φ) = M(φ0) ⨿_{A_n×T} (A_n×Δ^n)"); simplicial formula from the mapping-simplex definition at the start of §3.2.2 and Remarks 3.2.2.1–3.2.2.2, pp.178–180. Read online 2026-10-17. WANTED: archival copy under literature/. No Stacks tag states this simplicial result.

proof.text: Use the mapping-simplex construction of [def-coef-mapping-simplex-functor], which is exactly the formula in the statement. In each degree put $U_r=\{(\alpha,a):\alpha(r)<n\}$ and $V_r=\{(\alpha,a):\alpha(r)=n\}$ inside $M(A)_r$. Monotonicity says that $\alpha(r)<n$ is equivalent to every value of $\alpha$ lying in $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$. Consequently $U_r=(M_-)_r$, and $V_r$ is the disjoint union of copies of $(A_n)_r$ indexed by the remaining $\alpha$. The operators preserve $U$, since $\alpha\theta(s)\leq\alpha(r)<n$, so the indicated inclusion $j:M_-\to M(A)$ is simplicial.

source.place: Section 3.2.2, mapping-simplex definition, printed p.179; the decomposition in Proposition 3.2.2.10, p.183.

proof.text: Products and standard-simplex operators are degreewise by [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Write $k:A_n\times T\hookrightarrow A_n\times\Delta^n$ for the inclusion. For $\theta:[s]\to[r]$, write $i=\alpha(r)$ and $l=\alpha\theta(s)$. Applying the operator after $h_r$ gives $(\alpha\theta,t_{i,l}\theta^*(t_{n,i}a))=(\alpha\theta,t_{n,l}\theta^*a)$, since transitions are simplicial and $t_{i,l}t_{n,i}=t_{n,l}$. This equals $h_s(\theta^*a,\alpha\theta)$. If $\alpha$ lies in $T$, then so does $\alpha\theta$; the same calculation proves that $g$ is simplicial. Both composites $jg$ and $hk$ send $(a,\alpha)$ to $(\alpha,t_{n,\alpha(r)}a)$, so the square commutes.

source.place: Section 3.2.2 definition and Remarks 3.2.2.1–3.2.2.2, p.179; Proposition 3.2.2.10 proof, p.183.

proof.text: Let $Z$ be any small simplicial set and let $p:M_-\to Z$ and $q:A_n\times\Delta^n\to Z$ be simplicial maps satisfying $pg=qk$. Define a function $F_r:M(A)_r\to Z_r$ by $F_r(\alpha,a)=p_r(\alpha,a)$ if $\alpha(r)<n$, and $F_r(\alpha,a)=q_r(a,\alpha)$ if $\alpha(r)=n$. This has $Fj=p$. For $i=\alpha(r)<n$, compatibility gives $F_rh_r(a,\alpha)=p_rg_r(a,\alpha)=q_r(a,\alpha)$; for $i=n$, it gives $F_rh_r(a,\alpha)=q_r(a,\alpha)$ because $t_{n,n}=1$. Thus $Fh=q$ in every degree.

source.place: Proposition 3.2.2.10 proof, p.183: explicit universal-property expansion of its displayed mapping-simplex pushout.

proof.text: We check that $F$ commutes with every operator $\theta:[s]\to[r]$. If $i=\alpha(r)<n$, both sides are computed using $p$ and agree by its simpliciality. If $i=n$ and $l=\alpha\theta(s)=n$, both sides are computed using $q$ and agree by its simpliciality. In the remaining case $i=n$ and $l<n$, applying $F_s$ after the operator gives $p_s(\alpha\theta,t_{n,l}\theta^*a)=p_sg_s(\theta^*a,\alpha\theta)=q_s(\theta^*a,\alpha\theta)$, by $pg=qk$. This is $\theta^*q_r(a,\alpha)=\theta^*F_r(\alpha,a)$. These exhaust the cases, including faces that lose the final vertex; hence $F$ is a simplicial map.

source.place: Proposition 3.2.2.10 proof, p.183: explicit check across the attaching face from the operator formula on p.179.

proof.text: Every simplex of $U_r$ is in the image of $j_r$, and every simplex $(\alpha,a)$ of $V_r$ equals $h_r(a,\alpha)$. Therefore any simplicial map with composites $p,q$ is forced to equal the map $F$ just constructed. This proves the pushout universal property of [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] for the square of Step 2, with vertex $M(A)$. In particular this constructs a small pushout without appealing to a general colimit-existence theorem: the finite coproduct formula is small in every degree. For any chosen pushout $P$, its universal map $P\to M(A)$ and the universal map $M(A)\to P$ induced by its legs are inverse, since each composite agrees with the identity on both legs and uniqueness applies. This is exactly the canonical isomorphism in the statement.

source.place: Proposition 3.2.2.10 proof, p.183: universal property and canonical-isomorphism conclusion.

proof.text: The projections from $M_-$ and $A_n\times\Delta^n$ to $\Delta^n$ both send a simplex with label $\alpha$ to $\alpha$. They agree on $A_n\times T$, and $j,h$ preserve this label, so the canonical isomorphism is over $\Delta^n$. For a commuting ladder $f_i:A_i\to B_i$, [def-coef-mapping-simplex-functor] gives $M(f)(\alpha,a)=(\alpha,f_{\alpha(r)}a)$. The identity $f_i t^A_{n,i}=t^B_{n,i}f_n$ makes the squares for $g$ and $h$ commute degreewise; the square for $j$ is restriction of the same formula. The two maps from the source pushout to $M(B)$ therefore agree on both legs, hence agree by Step 5. This proves naturality of the canonical isomorphism. No step used injectivity of a transition, a horn filler, or nonemptiness of any $A_i$.

source.place: Remarks 3.2.2.1 and 3.2.2.5, pp.179–180; naturality of the decomposition in Proposition 3.2.2.10, p.183.
